races.title: State House, District 89
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Mitchell Smith Setzer
cands.bio: Republican member of the North Carolina House of Representatives for District 89, in office since 1999. Business executive, Vice President of Smith Setzer & Sons, Inc. Graduate of UNC Greensboro. Has chaired the House Finance and Insurance committees.

endorsements.text: In 2014 his endorsements included the State Employees Association of North Carolina (SEANC).

cands.gaps: His birthplace, upbringing and the year he came to North Carolina were not found. No statements from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, land buying, growth, immigration, guns, abortion, schools or police were found. No documented deeds on those topics were found either. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026, and no campaign site or interview text was available. No controversies, foreign ties or public stances on data centers or development were found in the sources available. His full employment history beyond his role at Smith Setzer & Sons, Inc. was not found. The only background source was a single Ballotpedia page.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the North Carolina House since 1999, and has served on the Finance, Insurance and Ethics committees across many sessions. He is also a business executive, Vice President of Smith Setzer & Sons, Inc.
qual.why: About 27 years of prior legislative service plus business management experience place him in the high band. Committee chair roles were not counted toward the score.
qual.label: About 27 years of prior legislative service plus business management experience place him in the high band. Committee chair roles were not counted toward the score.

cands.name: Robert (Spider) Thompson
cands.bio: Retired public school teacher (36 years), coach and athletic administrator from western Iredell County. Graduated from Emory & Henry in 1984. Democratic candidate for North Carolina House District 89 in 2026, running against incumbent Mitchell Setzer (R). Has not held elected office.
cands.gaps: We could not confirm where Thompson was born or raised, or the year he moved to North Carolina. He has no legislative or elected record, so there are no past actions to report. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws or abortion. Nothing we found documents controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements beyond three voter-guide groups listed on Ballotpedia. The last section of his campaign issues page (government accountability) was cut off, so we left out anything it may say.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He worked 36 years as a public school teacher, coach and athletic administrator, according to his campaign site and Ballotpedia survey. No legislative, local elected or budget-writing office appears in the sources.
qual.why: His long career in public education bears on education policy and school funding. The sources show no prior elected service, law or policy career, or business ownership, and the administrator role is within schools.
qual.label: His long career in public education bears on education policy and school funding. The sources show no prior elected service, law or policy career, or business ownership, and the administrator role is within schools.

land-for-floridians.evidence: Says he will push to give families who plan to live in a home a fair first shot at buying it and to shine a light on corporate buyers of starter homes. He gives no specific ban or tax proposal.
